newsitem.title: INDIA: India says to introduce 14-day Treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: India says to introduce 14-day Treasury bills.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday that it has decided to introduce the auction of 14-day Treasury bills.
The government said in a statement that the bills could be purchased by any person resident in India, including individuals, firms, companies, corporate bodies and institutions.
State governments, eligible provident funds and the Nepal Rastra Bank will be allowed to bid in auction on a "non-competitive" basis, it said.
The bills will be issued and repaid only in Bombay. There will be no notified amount for auctions, it said.
It said the bills will be issued for a minimum amount of 25,000 rupees and multiples thereof. The bills will be issued at a discounted price.
The minimum offer price, or cut-off price, above which bids will be accepted will be announced on the day of the auction, it said.
"The bills would form part of the borrowings of the government of India," it said, adding that they would be an approved investment for the purposes of the statutory liquidity ratio.
